legend.lines: one JSON object per line; dispatch on the TOP-LEVEL `kind`. `kind` is also the discriminator inside dtype trees, so a consumer that greps a line for "kind" instead of parsing it will mis-dispatch.
legend.line_kinds: header, dtype, layout, metadata, file_stats, zone_map, rows, null_counts
legend.null: JSON null, and nothing else ever is
legend.integer: decimal string, so u64/i64 extremes survive JSON
legend.float: {bits: hex of the raw IEEE bytes (NORMATIVE), dec: decimal, special: Infinity|-Infinity|NaN when the value is not finite}. `dec` spells the infinities `Infinity`/`-Infinity` so both Rust and .NET parse it; when the two ever disagree, `bits` wins.
legend.utf8: {b64: standard base64 of the UTF-8 BYTES, len: byte length, char_count: Unicode scalar count}. len != char_count wherever the value is not ASCII.
legend.struct: JSON object keyed by field name, in schema order
legend.map: JSON array of {key, value} objects, in stored order
legend.extension: the storage value; the extension id and metadata are in the dtype line
legend.rows: each `rows` line holds up to 128 values; row index = `from` + position in `v`
legend.null_counts: per field path, rows that are null there OR under a null ancestor struct. The path is `.`-joined field names from the root; the root itself is the empty string.
legend.layout.array_tree: on a vortex.flat node, the serialized ARRAY encoding tree inside that leaf, child order preserved. Absent on non-flat nodes.
legend.zone_map.aggregate_details: per aggregate, `precision`: `exact` for vortex.min/max/null_count/nan_count, `bound` for vortex.bounded_min/bounded_max — a bound is NOT a value, and a bounded entry with `unknown: true` carries no bound at all.
legend.metadata: user metadata segments in stored order; `b64` is "" for a present-but-empty segment and the key is simply absent when there is no such segment.
